newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - Swedish Nov CPI to fall 0.2 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Swedish Nov CPI to fall 0.2 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Swedish consumer prices were expected to fall 0.1 percent in November, giving a year-on-year fall of 0.2 percent in the latest 12 month period, a poll of 15 economists showed on Thursday.
Forecasts ranged from a fall of 0.2 percent to no change for the month, for year-on-year figures forecasts ranged from a fall of 0.3 percent to no change.
Economists forecast consumer prices would rise 0.8 percent on average for full-year 1996. Forecasts ranged from 0.7 percent to 0.8 percent.
In October the CPI index was unchanged from September to give a minus 0.1 percent year-on-year rate, the first time for 37 years that Sweden has fallen into deflation.
Statistics Sweden, Sweden's official statistics bureau, is due to publish the figure on December 12 at 0815 GMT.

Sources in the survey were Aragon, Carnegie, Consensus, Den Danske Bank, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland, J P Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Nordbanken, PaineWebber, S-E-Banken, Transferator, Union Bank of Switzerland, Unibank Markets.
